notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market SaaS (product analytics) building a conversational product + personalized search/ranking for enterprise customers. PLG motion but switching to contractual dedicated infra for performance guarantees.
- Started with Redwood hosted API for rapid prototyping (Q4 2025). Positive: latency profiles good at small scale; need predictable throughput and data isolation for larger accounts.
POC ask (current):
- Run Dedicated POC: 3-node GPU pool (reserved during business hours), 2-week canary then scale to full POC. Evaluate canary routing, model variant fallbacks, and region failover.
- Success metrics: p95 latency <= 200ms for chat generation (short prompts), throughput 30-50 RPS sustained, end-to-end 99.9% availability during business hours, token cost < $0.0013 equivalent on target workload.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key wrapping, audit log export to Splunk. EU data-residency for customers in EU (some data flow must stay in eu-west-1).
Technical notes from scoping call 2026-02-14 (Diego + Veridian Eng):
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic to Dedicated canary nodes behind Redwood routing policy. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 3 days if no regression.
- Fallback routing: default to hosted-api model variant (smaller quantized model) if Dedicated capacity degraded or GPU OOM. Policy to failover by latency spike detection (>2x baseline) OR error rate >1%.
- Model variants for POC: primary = redwood-quant-70b (fp16/quantized), fallback = redwood-8b-quant. Evaluation to include quality checks on top-k tokens and hallucination rate on 200-case prompt set.
- Region failover: primary eu-west-1 (for EU customers), fallback us-east-1; test cross-region routing and effect on latency + cache warm-up. KV-cache warming plan documented in Drive deck.
- Rollback: automated canary rollback if quality/regression metrics breach thresholds (BLEU/Rouge drop >5% on eval set OR user-facing error increase). SE will push a rollback runbook into POC runbook.
Commercial / Pricing:
- Pricing ask: committed reserved capacity estimate (monthly) vs burst billing for peak hours. Veridian wants a stepped downseat discount after month 3 if network stable. Need clearer burst pricing for unpredictable nightly batch jobs.
Other items and quotes:
- CTO: "We need deterministic tail latency and a clear rollback strategy before migrating customers."
- PM: wants per-route cost telemetry and token-level billing in console.

Open decisions:
- Exact node sizing and GPU type (A10G vs A100). SE to provide benchmark matrix week of 2026-03-03.
- Whether PII must be redacted before sending to hosted fallback model (privacy/legal ask).
